notes.name: Doug Treadwell
notes.body:
@alicia.palmer — QA heads-up on how to actually reach these cards, since the intake gating is narrower than it looks and a "no card appeared" result is easy to misread as a bug.

> **Correction (edited).** My original version of this note told you Sidekick was the *easy* repro path. That was wrong — the Sidekick weather-descriptors step is **not in the flow at all** any more (details below). Please read the FNOL section as the only live path. Sorry for the misdirection.

The two Temperature factor cards fire off user-reported `HOT` / `COLD` weather descriptors, which live in **two different places** depending on the module.

**Sidekick — not reachable on a new claim.** The `weatherUserDescriptors_v2` step ("To the best of your recollection, what was the weather at the time of the incident?") wrote `HOT`/`COLD` onto the reporting party, but the rule that put it in the flow was **removed on 2026-05-11** by AUTO-7001 ("Removing SK options", 70ade66f) — it was also delisted from the voice-intake step inventory in the same commit. The step object and its `v2Registry` entry still exist, but no module wires it, so **no new Sidekick claim can populate this field**. Only Sidekick claims filed *before* that date can carry it, and even then only ones classified `WEATHER` (the old rule's filter). So please don't spend time trying to drive a fresh Sidekick claim to these cards — if you want to exercise that branch it needs a pre-May-11 weather claim, or seeded data.

**FNOL / standard — the live path.** The `incidentWeatherUserDescriptors` step only renders in one of these cases:
1. You answer **"Nope" 🙁** to *"Just making sure we're on the same page – does this describe the weather at the time of the …?"*, **or**
2. no forecast could be derived for the claim, in which case you get a single **"Got it"** button that records the same thing.

And even when it renders, the option list depends on classification: on a **WEATHER**-classified claim with weather-collision enhancements enabled the list swaps to the weather-related descriptors, which contain **no Hot/Cold at all**. Hot/Cold only appear in the default (full) list.

Also note **theft / vandalism / rodent-damage** claims skip the weather-forecast confirm step entirely, so they never reach the descriptors step and can never produce these cards.

**First Contact / intelligent_investigation** has no weather-descriptors step. An FC claim shows the card only if the originating FNOL collected it.

Other things worth exercising:
- **Both cards can appear at once** — the question is multi-select, so Hot + Cold together is expected, not a duplicate-card bug.
- With no reporter name resolvable the copy falls back to *"The reporting party said it was hot"* — also intended.

@jorgecoello — two doc items fall out of this:
1. The sources doc's Sidekick section states the SK step "persists the same enum onto the **reporting party**" in the present tense, and the MR description says "Sidekick reads the reporting party's weather descriptors". Given AUTO-7001 unwired that step, that branch now only serves historical claims — worth saying so explicitly, since as written it reads as a live second source.
2. The "Non-obvious details / gotchas" section frames the FNOL gating as *"weather-loss claims often will not have this card … on weather-classified FNOL with enhancements on"*, which understates it: on FNOL the descriptors step doesn't render **at all** unless the forecast was rejected or unavailable, regardless of classification.

notes.name: Jorge Coello

@alicia.palmer the repro path is in the sources doc now. Hot + Cold together and the

notes.name: Doug Treadwell
notes.body:
[NON-BLOCKING] **This section describes a step that is no longer in any flow** — the Sidekick branch is real but serves only historical claims, and the doc reads as though it's a live second source.

`weatherUserDescriptors_v2` still exists and is still in `V2_REGISTRY`, but the `rule({ key: 'weatherUserDescriptors', step: weatherUserDescriptors })` that put it in the Sidekick flow was deleted from `100-auto-sidekick.ts` on 2026-05-11 by **AUTO-7001 "Removing SK options"** (`70ade66f`) — the same commit also removed it from `AUTO_CLAIMS_NON_DATA_WORKFLOW_STEP_KEYS` in `autoClaimsIntakeInventory.ts`.

How I checked, in case it's worth re-verifying:
- On current `origin/master`, `rg weatherUserDescriptors apps/backend/src/workflows` returns only the step file itself and the `v2Registry` import — no module imports it into a rule.
- Registry membership isn't wiring: `V2_REGISTRY` is consumed only by `getStaticStepDefinitions()`, which publishes step-definition metadata and validation JSON schemas. A step reaches a flow only via a direct import + `rule({ key, step })` in a module.
- The rule that was removed also filtered on `otherClassification === WEATHER`, so even the historical data is limited to weather-classified Sidekick claims filed before that date.
- The only other backend references are read-side (loss-domain mapping, carrier payload builders). Nothing else writes `party.weatherUserDescriptors`.

So `party.weatherUserDescriptors` is effectively a **legacy field**: no new Sidekick claim can populate it, and the FNOL "reporter declined / had no forecast" route is the only way to produce these cards on a new claim.

To be clear about what this is and isn't: the code is **not wrong**. Reading the party field is still correct for pre-May-2026 weather claims, and I'd rather it be read than silently dropped. What needs fixing is the framing — three places currently assert a live second source:

1. **This section** — "The Sidekick `weatherUserDescriptors_v2` step persists the same enum onto the **reporting party**" (present tense). Suggest noting that the step was unwired by AUTO-7001 on 2026-05-11 and that this path now only covers claims filed before then.
2. **`$reportingPartyWeatherDescriptors`'s JSDoc** in `AutoIncidentWeatherAccessor.ts` — "Sidekick records weather descriptors on the reporting party" reads as current behavior. This is exactly the kind of non-obvious historical constraint that earns a JSDoc, so it's worth spelling out there rather than only here.
3. **The MR description** — "Sidekick reads the reporting party's weather descriptors" sits alongside the FNOL source as a peer.

Then there's a product call worth making explicitly rather than by default:

- **Keep the branch** (my suggestion) if pre-May-2026 weather claims still get looked at — it's cheap, already tested, and dropping it would silently lose those cards. Just label it as the legacy path in all three places above.
- **Drop it** if those claims are out of scope, which would also remove the fragment field, `$reportingPartyWeatherDescriptors`, the `in`-guard from my other comment, and 3 of the 9 tests — a decent simplification.

Either way, worth deciding on purpose. Happy to be wrong if AUTO-7001 was reverted somewhere I didn't look, or if there's a re-wiring in flight.

cc @alicia.palmer — this is why I corrected the repro steps in my other note; a fresh Sidekick claim can't reach these cards.

$reportingPartyWeatherDescriptors JSDoc, and the MR description all now cite

notes.name: Doug Treadwell
notes.body:
@jorgecoello — heads-up, not a change request: I've opened a question for Design and PM on the ticket, and it may generate a follow-up. **Nothing here blocks this MR** — what you built matches the AC and the Figma copy.

👉 [New comment on CV-1730 for @adam.peterson and @paul_rivera](https://linear.app/assured/issue/CV-1730/highlight-temperature-factor#comment-59c64862)

**The question:** should an *accepted* forecast temperature also produce these cards? Right now the descriptors multi-select only appears when the reporter answers "Nope" to the forecast-confirm step (or when no forecast could be derived). On the common path — "Yes, that's correct" — we never ask, so no Temperature factor card.

What makes it worth asking rather than obviously out of scope: that confirmation screen renders the actual temperature (`{forecast.temperature.toFixed(0)}°F` in `WeatherForecast.tsx`), so a reporter who accepts it has looked at "98°F" and affirmed it. Whether that counts as "Lisa said it was hot" is a product/design call, not an engineering one.

If they say yes, three things need their answers first — thresholds (Weston's 1 May comment on the ticket is still the open item there; the weather service's own `Hot`/`Frigid` condition codes are one way to avoid picking numbers), copy and attribution, and whether it extends CV-1730 or becomes a new ticket. I suggested a follow-up so this MR isn't held up.

Related, and the reason I raised it: combined with the Sidekick step being unwired (see my comment on `temperatureFactor.highlightFact.sources.md`), the cards as shipped will only appear on FNOL claims where the reporter rejected or lacked a forecast. That's a narrower slice than the ticket probably assumed, so it seemed worth surfacing to PM now rather than after someone asks why the highlight never shows up.

notes.name: Jorge Coello
notes.body:
Agreed, this MR stays on user-reported HOT/COLD. I documented under "Not used" that
confirming the forecast never collects HOT/COLD, so a missing card there is intake
behavior, not a CVI bug. Happy to take the follow-up once thresholds and copy are
decided.
